detections.evidence_quote: Is it dangerous to have metal on you when you get an MRI
detections.summary: Hosts discuss MRI safety with metal, including dental restorations, and how MRI magnets work.

detections.evidence_quote: you should not have any metal, even metal crowns in your mouth
detections.summary: Warns that MRI magnets can dislodge, bend or break metal dental crowns and restorations.

verification_candidates.claim_text: The vibration from MRI magnets can dislodge, bend, and break dental restorations.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: the vibration can dislodge, bend, and break the dental restoration just from the magnets
verification_candidates.rationale: A specific safety claim about dental work during MRI that could be checked against imaging safety guidance.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Loose metal objects can injure you during an MRI.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: loose metal objects can injure you as that
verification_candidates.rationale: General MRI safety claim that is checkable.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Having a metal plate in your head or fillings in your teeth makes someone a bad candidate for an MRI.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: I would think if you have a metal plate in your head or you got fillings in your teeth, then you would be a bad candidate
verification_candidates.rationale: A safety and eligibility claim about metal implants and dental fillings in MRI.
